featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want a short escape from Mumbai’s endless traffic, crowded streets, and fast-paced routine, then Madh Island offers exactly that. Tucked away on the northern edge of the city, this coastal destination feels surprisingly detached from Mumbai despite being within city limits. The journey itself whether by road or via the ferry near Versova Beach adds to the charm and makes the place feel like a hidden getaway.

What stands out most about Madh Island is its peaceful atmosphere. Unlike Juhu or Girgaon Chowpatty, the beaches here are far less commercialized and considerably less crowded. Places such as Erangal Beach, Dana Pani Beach, and Madh Beach are perfect for long walks, watching sunsets, or simply sitting by the sea and enjoying the sound of the waves. The rustic fishing villages, coconut trees, old bungalows, and coastal roads give the area a unique charm that is becoming increasingly rare in Mumbai.

The island is not without its flaws. Several visitors mention that cleanliness can vary depending on the season and crowd levels, and some stretches of the beach may have litter or a slight smell associated with fishing activities. Road conditions and traffic during peak hours can also be frustrating, especially while leaving after sunset. However, most people agree that the tranquility, greenery, and open spaces more than compensate for these shortcomings.

Overall, Madh Island is one of Mumbai’s most underrated destinations. It is not a luxury beach town or a perfect tourist hotspot, but that is exactly what makes it special. If you are looking for a peaceful evening, a scenic drive, a weekend staycation, or simply a place to disconnect from the chaos of city life, Madh Island delivers a refreshing experience that feels worlds away from Mumbai while still being a part of it.

Marve Jetty serves as one of the gateway connecting the mainland to Gorai Island through a quick ferry ride. The drive to the jetty from the surrounding suburbs is good but you might face traffic on weekends and on busy evenings.

Once you arrive, the beach area welcomes you with a vibrant stretch of food stalls offering everything from classic chaat to flavourful seafood preparations (must try fried fish). And if you’re someone who appreciates a truly fresh catch, consider buying fish from the local Koli community. Their produce is fresh, reasonably priced, and supports the traditional fishing families who have lived by these shores for generations.

Parking facilities have also improved greatly in recent times. Visitors will find ample and convenient parking space for both two-wheelers and four-wheelers, making the overall experience smooth and stress-free.

featured_reviews.name: Ragini Dev
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a woman living in the hustle of Mumbai, finding a pocket of peace is a luxury, and that's exactly what Marve Beach offers. It’s not about the thrill of water sports; it’s about the sheer calmness and clarity I find here.
I often visit in the late afternoon, and the primary appeal is the relative serenity. Unlike the constant commotion of Juhu or Chowpatty, Marve feels almost residential—a true suburban retreat. I appreciate that I can take a long, leisurely stroll barefoot without constantly bumping into crowds. It feels much safer and more comfortable to simply walk, reflect, and enjoy my own company here.
The highlight, without a doubt, is the sunset. Marve offers an absolutely unspoiled view of the sun sinking into the Arabian Sea. Watching the sky explode in shades of burnt orange and soft lavender while the tide gently laps the shore is truly a grounding experience. It’s a photographer’s dream and a perfect moment for a bit of personal meditation.
Beyond the natural beauty, I love the slice of local life it provides. You’ll see the local Koli fishing community bringing their boats in, which adds an authentic, rustic charm. I also find the area around the jetty fascinating, with the old Portuguese church and the visible naval base (INS Hamla) giving it a unique, historical flavor.
Marve also acts as a wonderful mini-adventure hub. The ferry service to Manori Island (famously known as Mini Goa) or Madh Island is a brilliant option for a quick, unplanned getaway. You can easily spend an hour relaxing here and then hop on a boat for a whole new experience.
Finally, you can't leave without indulging in the local treats. A small chaat stall offering spicy bhel puri or a perfectly roasted ear of corn makes the end of the evening perfect.
In my book, Marve Beach is a precious find. It’s a less commercialized, more tranquil space that provides a safe and picturesque backdrop for much-needed relaxation, making it my preferred coastal escape in the city. Just remember to visit on a weekday or early morning if you want the maximum peace, and leave the swimming to the fish—the strong currents here are no joke!

featured_reviews.name: Geeta maa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Exotic Notes
Introduction
I have been an ardent food lover all my life. I have enjoyed cooking, and
cherished feeding people just as much. However, for the first time ever I was
invited to review a residential property, cosily tucked away at the Mudh Island in
Mumbai. Karan Raheja was one of the most humble hosts I have ever come
across. It was very nice of him to take time out and tour me around the Raheja
Exotica Sorento.
On the way
The journey to the property was a breeze. I hopped on to Versova Jetty, after
which a brief speedboat ride took me to the other end of the jetty. The Raheja’s
specially appointed a chauffer driven vehicle to drive me to the complex.
Pristine beauty
My jaws simply dropped at the awe inspiring architectural marvel that enhanced
the island. The Raheja Exotica Sorento, could be typically named as the Island of
pleasure. The greenery on the site gripped me. The Arabian Sea hugs the island
rendering to its unique character and feature. The cooling sea breeze kisses you
as you take a walk on the lush green lawns on the property. The complex is
squeaky clean, and has employed people round the clock to maintain the same.
The European Marvel
The eco-system is complete; sprawling over 32 acres of land. The two 36
storeyed, towers touch the pinnacles of the sky overlooking the limitless
expanses of the Arabian Sea. The homes are fully furnished comprising of state of
the art facilities. You could call them designer homes too. The complex houses 2,
3, and 4 BHK houses. The architecture is a clear marriage of the Indian and
European chic elements. While you are cut off from the hustle and bustle of city
life, the cooing from the faraway metro train keeps you going.
Location and Proximity
The location proves challenging at first, but the site has been developed after the
careful consideration of the future infrastructure around the property. This
simply means we are looking at,  5 Minutes from Versova by operational ferry service.  25 Minutes by road from Mindspace, Malad (W).  Proposed bridge connecting Versova to Madh, will considerably reduce
travel time.  Propose Coastal Road that will make it easier to travel to South Mumbai.
The Facilities
The property has it all! Right from a brilliant swimming pool to banquet halls to a
well facilitated gymnasium, a fantastic spa, and a lot more! Of I cannot overlook
the supermarket that stocks on supplies on a regular basis. A spacious
amphitheatre, café, 24/7-concierge service, a well-equipped business centre and
a lot more! Access to the banquet hall is only limited to members residing on the
premises and their guests during a celebration. Security is deeply entrenched on
the premises, limiting outsiders to certain areas only. The services are well
rounded making the property investment worthy for expats and NRI’s too. The
expected residents are very cosmopolitan in origin.
Café
The café serves lip-smacking delights that included everything from the luscious
‘Palak Paneer’, ‘Jeera Aloo’, an array of ‘Raitas’, the ‘deep red beetroot halwa’,
‘Rasgulla’, orange juice, and a lot more.
End Note
While I was there I was transported to tranquillity and calm. I was almost on the
verge of weeping, as I was to leave. I hope to have a home in the wondrous place
and spend the latter part of my life by the cool breeze of the Arabian Sea far away
from the city mayhem.

featured_reviews.name: Nidhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited the Versova Jetty and found it to be a very unique and important local travel spot. This jetty connects Versova to Madh Island (also known as Mud Island), which is home to the vibrant Koli fishing community and some beautiful residential areas.
What makes this place interesting is how it blends everyday life with a bit of Mumbai’s glamour. Many people, including residents from Madh Island and even celebrities like Archana Puran Singh and many other use this jetty to travel towards Andheri and Versova.
The ferry ride is very affordable (just around ₹10), making it a convenient option for daily commuters. However, it can get quite crowded, especially during peak hours, so be prepared for a bit of rush.
Overall, it’s not just a transport point but an experience of Mumbai’s local culture, community life, and coastal charm. Recommended for those who want to explore a different side of the city.
